# Angular Component Standards

**Load at**: Module 6 (Component Implementation)
**Applies to**: All Angular components generated by the `angular-ui` agent

---

## 1. Component Structure

### Decorator
```typescript
@Component({
  selector: 'app-[screen-name]',    // always 'app-' prefix
  standalone: true,                  // default for Angular 21+
  imports: [
    // Only import what is USED in the template
    // Never import entire modules (e.g. CommonModule) if only one pipe is needed
  ],
  templateUrl: './[screen-name].component.html',
  styleUrl: './[screen-name].component.scss',
  changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush  // use when possible
})
```

### Class Structure (in order)
```typescript
export class [ScreenName]Component implements OnInit {
  // 1. Injected services (private readonly, via inject())
  private readonly router = inject(Router);

  // 2. Inputs and Outputs
  @Input() entityId?: string;
  @Output() cancelled = new EventEmitter<void>();

  // 3. Reactive form (if form screen)
  protected readonly form = new FormGroup({ ... });

  // 4. State (signals or BehaviorSubjects)
  protected isLoading = false;
  protected errorMessage = '';

  // 5. Lifecycle hooks
  ngOnInit(): void { }

  // 6. Public/protected event handlers
  protected onSubmit(): void { }
  protected onCancel(): void { }

  // 7. Private helpers
  private loadData(): void { }
}
```

### Access Modifiers
- `private readonly` — injected services, never accessed in template
- `protected` — methods and properties bound in template
- `public` — only for `@Input()`, `@Output()`, and methods called by parent
- Never use `public` for internal state or event handlers

---

## 2. Dependency Injection

Use `inject()` function — NOT constructor injection:
```typescript
// ✅ Correct
private readonly userService = inject(UserService);

// ❌ Wrong
constructor(private userService: UserService) {}
```

Use `DestroyRef` for teardown in standalone components:
```typescript
private readonly destroyRef = inject(DestroyRef);

// In subscription:
someObservable$
  .pipe(takeUntilDestroyed(this.destroyRef))
  .subscribe(...);
```

---

## 3. Reactive Forms

Use `ReactiveFormsModule`. Never use template-driven forms for multi-field screens.

```typescript
// FormGroup with typed controls
protected readonly form = new FormGroup({
  name: new FormControl<string>('', {
    nonNullable: true,
    validators: [Validators.required, Validators.maxLength(100)]
  }),
  email: new FormControl<string>('', {
    nonNullable: true,
    validators: [Validators.required, Validators.email]
  }),
});

// Access controls safely
get nameControl() { return this.form.controls.name; }
```

Validators to apply based on Figma field rules:
| Figma rule | Validator |
|-----------|-----------|
| Required | `Validators.required` |
| Max length N | `Validators.maxLength(N)` |
| Email format | `Validators.email` |
| Min value N | `Validators.min(N)` |
| Pattern / regex | `Validators.pattern(...)` |

---

## 4. Template Standards

### Control Flow (Angular 21+ syntax)
```html
@if (condition) { ... }
@else { ... }

@for (item of items; track item.id) { ... }

@switch (value) {
  @case ('a') { ... }
  @default { ... }
}
```
Do NOT use `*ngIf`, `*ngFor`, `*ngSwitch` — they are legacy syntax.

### Async Pipe
Prefer `async` pipe over manual subscriptions in templates:
```html
@if (items$ | async; as items) {
  @for (item of items; track item.id) {
    <div>{{ item.name }}</div>
  }
}
```

### Data Binding
- `[property]` — one-way property binding (component → DOM)
- `(event)` — event binding (DOM → component)
- `[(ngModel)]` — two-way (ONLY for simple cases; prefer reactive forms)
- `{{ expression }}` — interpolation

### Template Variables
Use `#ref` sparingly — only for accessing DOM elements or child component APIs.

---

## 5. Error Display Pattern

For reactive form validation errors:
```html
<mat-form-field appearance="outline">
  <mat-label>Name</mat-label>
  <input matInput formControlName="name" />
  @if (form.controls.name.hasError('required') && form.controls.name.touched) {
    <mat-error>Name is required</mat-error>
  }
  @if (form.controls.name.hasError('maxlength')) {
    <mat-error>Name cannot exceed 100 characters</mat-error>
  }
</mat-form-field>
```

For async/global errors:
```html
@if (errorMessage) {
  <div role="alert" aria-live="assertive" class="error-banner">
    {{ errorMessage }}
  </div>
}
```

---

## 6. Loading State

```html
<!-- Show spinner while loading -->
@if (isLoading) {
  <div class="loading-container" aria-label="Loading" role="status">
    <mat-spinner diameter="40"></mat-spinner>
  </div>
}

<!-- Disable submit button during loading -->
<button mat-raised-button color="primary" [disabled]="isLoading || form.invalid">
  @if (isLoading) { Saving... } @else { Submit }
</button>
```

---

## 7. What NOT to Do

- Do NOT use `any` type without a comment explaining why it cannot be avoided
- Do NOT subscribe manually without using `takeUntilDestroyed` or `async` pipe
- Do NOT hardcode colours, fonts, or pixel values in component SCSS (use CSS variables or Material theme)
- Do NOT call service methods directly in the template (bind to component methods instead)
- Do NOT use `setTimeout` for anything that can be achieved with RxJS operators
- Do NOT leave `console.log` calls in committed code
- Do NOT import entire `CommonModule` — import only the specific directives needed

---

## 8. SCSS Standards

```scss
// Component SCSS: use BEM-like naming
.screen-name-container {
  padding: var(--spacing-lg, 24px);
  max-width: 960px;
  margin: 0 auto;

  &__section { ... }
  &__actions { ... }
}

// Use CSS custom properties for theming
.error-text {
  color: var(--mat-sys-error);  // Angular Material system token
}

// Never hardcode:
// ❌ color: #b00020;
// ✅ color: var(--mat-sys-error);
```
